candidates.evidence: Two in-plane/out-of-plane modes at 383.8 (E2g1) and 403.3 cm-1 (A1g), difference 19.5 cm-1, match 2H-MoS2 at 532 nm. Si substrate line at 520.9 cm-1 also present. No other common TMD fits these two positions: WS2 is near 355/418, MoSe2 near 243/287, WSe2 near 250.

hint_reasoning: material_hint is null, so there is no stated material to check against. The identification comes from the peak positions alone.

peaks.source: Position and FWHM from Lorentzian fit over 355-430 cm-1 (sigma 1.03, +/-0.02 cm-1). Assignment from Lee et al., ACS Nano 4, 2695 (2010) and Li et al., Adv. Funct. Mater. 22, 1385 (2012): E2g1 near 384 cm-1 for MoS2.

Position and FWHM from Lorentzian fit over 355-430 cm-1 (sigma 1.91, +/-0.05 cm-1). Assignment from Lee et al., ACS Nano 4, 2695 (2010) and Li et al., Adv. Funct. Mater. 22, 1385 (2012): A1g near 403-405 cm-1 for monolayer MoS2.
Position from fit over 495-545 cm-1. Literature Si first-order Raman line at about 520.7 cm-1 (Temple and Hathaway, PRB 7, 3685, 1973), so the offset is about +0.2 cm-1.

properties.name: layers
properties.source: A1g-E2g separation of 19.5 cm-1 (calibration-independent). Literature 532 nm trend (Lee et al. 2010; Li et al. 2012): monolayer about 18.5-19.5 cm-1, bilayer about 20-21 cm-1, bulk about 24-25 cm-1. The value sits at the top of the monolayer range and below the bilayer range.

properties.name: phase
properties.source: E2g1 and A1g pair only. Literature: 2H-MoS2 shows these two modes; 1T' would show additional low-frequency modes around 150-230 cm-1, none of which are resolved here (Lee et al. 2010).

artifacts.type: possible single-pixel spike, unconfirmed (about +600 counts, about 4 sigma of noise, isolated with no broadening; not reported as a peak)

citations: Lee, C. et al. ACS Nano 4, 2695 (2010) - MoS2 Raman modes and thickness dependence of E2g1 and A1g separation
Li, H. et al. Adv. Funct. Mater. 22, 1385 (2012) - from bulk to monolayer MoS2, Raman evolution with layer number
Temple, P.A. and Hathaway, C.E. PRB 7, 3685 (1973) - Si first-order Raman line near 520.7 cm-1
limits: Material: the two-peak pattern at 383.8 and 403.3 cm-1 with a 19.5 cm-1 separation identifies MoS2. Literature values are quoted from memory and should be checked against the papers before use.

Layer count: 1 layer is most likely, but the result is not decisive. A bilayer would give a separation of about 20-21 cm-1, and the measured 19.5 cm-1 is close to that edge. Single-spot data cannot exclude 2 layers. A second spot, a photoluminescence check, or a comparison against a reference monolayer on the same substrate would settle it.
Layer count is inferred from one number. Peak intensity ratios are not used because they depend on focus, substrate, and laser power.

E2g1 FWHM (2.06 cm-1) is narrower than usual for MoS2 on SiO2 and is only about 3 data points across the peak (0.68 cm-1 step). Its width is poorly constrained. The Si line has FWHM 3.5 cm-1, so the instrument resolution is not better than about 3 cm-1.
Absolute positions are good to about 0.3 cm-1 with the Si calibration. The A1g-E2g separation does not depend on calibration.
Weak MoS2 modes (2LA(M) near 450, LA(M) near 227, E1g near 286) are not resolved above the noise (about 145 counts per point). Their absence is weak evidence for a thin flake, not a proof.
The single 453.5 cm-1 excursion could be a cosmic-ray remnant or noise, and it cannot be assigned to 2LA(M) with this data.
Polarization dependence is not classified because this is a single spectrum, not an angle-resolved series.
The broad background (about 2500-4500 counts) was modeled only as a smooth low-order polynomial. Any broad SiO2 or fluorescence band is not separated out.
